content.text: Cloud computing has fundamentally transformed how organizations build, deploy, and operate software systems. Rather than provisioning physical hardware months in advance, teams can now spin up global infrastructure in minutes, pay only for what they consume, and scale elastically to meet demand. The major cloud providers — AWS, Azure, and GCP — offer hundreds of managed services that abstract away operational complexity, but this abundance creates its own challenge: choosing the right services, architecting for reliability, and managing costs requires deep expertise that goes beyond clicking through a console.

This multi-page guide covers cloud computing from a senior engineer's perspective, focusing on AWS as the dominant platform while highlighting patterns that apply across providers. The content is production-oriented, emphasizing architectural decisions, failure modes, cost implications, and operational best practices that distinguish experienced cloud engineers from those who merely deploy to the cloud.

items: AWS Core Services — EC2, S3, Lambda, RDS, DynamoDB, SQS, SNS, and CloudFront — the foundational building blocks for any AWS architecture
Serverless Patterns — Lambda architecture, cold starts, event-driven design, Step Functions, and serverless databases for building scalable applications without managing servers
Infrastructure as Code — Terraform, CloudFormation, Pulumi, state management, modules, and drift detection for reproducible, version-controlled infrastructure
Cloud Architecture Patterns — Multi-region deployments, disaster recovery strategies, cost optimization techniques, and the AWS Well-Architected Framework
